title: The view from the top
hookLine: from here you can see every path and the one direction they face
tomorrow: Jordan drives Amira to the airport. what did her grandma tell her?

lines: ONE THING THEY ALL DO THE SAME.
cards: The night before you leave home is always the same: a suitcase that won't zip, a charger you can't find, a family group chat that's about to get busier. Everyone is about to be somewhere different.
A dad at his coffee shop, a grandmother on her couch, a little cousin at school, a best friend at a college three hours away. Scattered across a map.
And yet, from high enough up, there's one thing they all still do the same way.

teach.b: They face the same way. The qibla is the direction of prayer, toward the Ka'ba in Mecca. In every mosque, a niche in the wall, the mihrab, points to it.
From a kitchen in Houston, it's one angle. From a dorm in Chicago, a slightly different one. Zoom out far enough and the rows of people praying across the world all turn toward a single point.

Here's the picture to tell a friend tonight: around the Ka'ba itself, the rows can't all face one wall, so they become circles, people praying toward the center, facing one another across it. That's the view from the top.
Every path visible, and every path turned one way.
The Qur'an widens it further: "Unto Allah belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance." The qibla gathers the body; God isn't confined to it.

teach.h: NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.
teach.b: And then it widens it again, to everyone: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another."
One human family, made different on purpose, so the knowing would be worth doing.
For someone about to scatter, that's what this path gives. Not a promise that everyone stays in one house.
A direction everyone shares, wherever the suitcase ends up, and a reason to know the people from the other tribes along the way.

how: Muslims everywhere face the qibla, toward the Ka'ba in Mecca, when they pray; mosques mark it with a mihrab, and travelers find it with a compass or a phone.

games.q: what does “the view from the top” mean?
o: a mountain in Mecca where pilgrims pray
the moment you finally stop climbing for good
every path seen at once, all facing one way

games.q: what's in the view — tap the pairs.
p: the niche that points the way
nations and tribes, to know one another

s: around the Ka'ba, people pray in rings, facing one another across it
rows that face one point become circles around it.
the Qur'an says God is found only in the direction of the qibla
2:115: whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance.
the Qur'an says people were made nations and tribes to know one another

games.q: on a road trip, your phone dies at prayer time in a rest-stop parking lot, and you can't find the qibla. what fits today?
o: skip it; without the exact direction the prayer won't count.
make your best guess and pray; wherever you turn, God is there.
face east, because the qibla is east from everywhere.
games.why: 2:115: unto Allah belong the East and the West. you do your honest best with the direction, and the prayer goes on.

practice: Find a window or a doorway and look out, as far as you can see. Let one person come to mind behind each roof or road you can see, people you know and people you don't.
Then turn toward the qibla if you know it, or simply stay where you are, and sit and look until the time is up.

wordCard.voice: The view from the top: every path in sight, and the one direction they all face.

orig.note: Arabic: the direction faced in prayer, toward the Ka'ba.

carryVoice: Something to keep: everything faces him, even a family scattered across a map. Fourteen of fifteen, one step left.
